pages.transcription:
New York, Aug 11th, 41

Dear Mamma,
Yesterday your letter of July 27th with the
photos which I will give to Eva in a little album as
you suggested. I liked the one of you with Manfred very
very much and would love to have it. Please send it to us,
I suppose already c/o Editora Guanabara, 132 rua
Ouvidor, Rio - for we have now the tickets and nearly all the
necessary papers and probably leave Friday. Just as last
year it was the worst to come to a decision; now that it
is made and only unforeseen events will change our plans
we feel better and more ready and willing to go. -
About Eva you need not worry - I probably shall miss her
more than she will miss us in spite of all her liking of
us. And I am very glad that we spent the last weeks
so near to her and saw her frequently. To-morrow she
goes to our cousin Elizabeth for a few days and
I hope she will like it. We shall certainly see her
before we go and Yonkers is even nearer than Croton
should we suddenly have some spare time in these
last few days. It is a pity to leave almost on her
birthday but I shall try to leave her some nice
present and she will have a party at Amity Hall.
In a few weeks they will move to the new house
and I suppose the "big" children like her will
have an important part in it. Mrs. Sch. will get
a prospectus with pictures so that you will have a
fair idea what the new place looks like. It is a
grand property, a beautiful big house and perfectly
suitable for an establishment like that.
Yesterday Foges suddenly phoned and we were
with him for more than an hour. He brought your
regards and tried to tell as much as he could. On
the whole I found, however, that he knew most about
Marte about whose excellent qualities he was quite
enthusiastic. He must have dined there frequently!
pages.notes: Handschriftlicher Brief auf weißem Papier. Tinte violett. Sehr gut lesbar.

pages.transcription:
2)
He intends to return in September and will report to you, I
suppose. But I hope that before him Mr. Honig will have
called upon you - he knows us better and we were together
quite frequently while he was here. -
We are terribly busy these last days and besides
this have some shopping to do as all clothing is either
not good or expensive in Rio. And it is typically Ame-
rican that it is already difficult for me to find
summer dresses. The sales started when we were away
and the shops are practically sold out and at this very
moment busy with selling furs and winter things. For
Stefan it is easier because the mens' sales began
much later and are still on. About the sudden crisis
in silk stockings you may have read in the papers. It
was quite a panic when the silk import from Japan
was stopped, the women rushed out to buy and hoard
and it is with a kind of horror that they foresee the
necessity of wearing cotton stockings. I cannot get very
excited about it and actually bought less than I would
otherwise have done as the prices already nearly doubled.
I suppose if you get along without silk stockings, the Western
Hemisphere will also be able to do so. By the way, I
carefully studied what you wear on the photos but I did
not recognise anything except the checked grandmothers-sheet
dress. However I recognized Millers antoize trousers and
suppose they are still the same pair. This reminds me to
write that of course you have full authority to give away
and make use of mine and Stefan's clothes. I hope you have
done so already! - I am terribly sorry that Mr. Wilmot keeps on
bothering you with our affairs. We never meant it to be thus
but thought that all you would have to do would be to
furnish him all the statements and documents that come
in without worrying about any details, especially as you know
much less about our "business" than he does. - I am anxious
to hear whether Manfred already has his new job and where and
how and when it is. A pity it could not be in Bath.
Warmest greetings Lotte.
